title: compact-auth-stream-suppress-and-lightweight-retry-surface-v1.29.0
author: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: This PR reduces auth handshake surface area in the TS SDK, introduces a stream suppression flag to avoid noisy reconnect churn, exposes a lightweight retry preset for streaming consumers, and bumps the package to v1.29.0. Motivation: parity with recent Python/Go ergonomics changes (lighter auth choreography, deterministic retry presets) and to prevent transient reconnect storms observed in high-throughput streaming scenarios. Key goals: 1) remove per-chunk re-auth ceremony in the hot path, 2) let consumers opt-in to "suppressReconnects" for chat/streaming clients to avoid aggressive back-and-forth on short failures, 3) publish a documented "light" retry preset tuned for sub-200ms median latency endpoints, and 4) micro-version bump and changelog update.
commits: a1b2c3d: introduce CompactAuth class and migrate connector handshake to cached token path
d4e5f6a: add suppressReconnects option on StreamingClient and runtime guard
b7c8d9e: implement lightweight retry preset (retry-light) and wire to streaming defaults
c0d1e2f: unit + integration tests for suppressed reconnect behavior and backoff correctness
e3f4a5b: docs: API reference, migration notes and changelog v1.29.0
review_comments: Evan Li: Great direction, can we ensure the CompactAuth instance is GC-friendly? I saw a retained Map in early runs.
Author (Aisha): Addressed — cleaned up token cache TTL and added weak refs for non-critical entries (see compactAuth.ts).
Marta Gomez: CI indicated a flaky expectation in the simulated latency test. Can we reduce timing sensitivity?
Author (Aisha): Adjusted test harness to use event-driven markers instead of fixed timers; added retry window helper to stabilize assertion.
Rajiv Menon: API ergonomics look good. One suggestion: rename suppressReconnects -> streamReconnectPolicy for future extensibility.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK v1.29.0: reduced auth handshake overhead for streaming, added 'suppressReconnects' opt-in to reduce reconnect churn under transient failures, introduced 'retry-light' preset for latency-sensitive streams, documented migration notes. No breaking changes expected; opt-in runtime behavior.
discussion_summary: Design tradeoff: default remains conservative (no suppression) to avoid hiding persistent auth faults; suppression is opt-in for apps tolerant of transient drops.
Performance: unit benchmarks show ~12% lower CPU per stream in steady-state due to fewer auth serialization paths.
Compatibility: brought TS behavior into alignment with Python/Go compact auth primitives; cross-sdk tests updated in separate coordination PRs.
